cases.description: New serializer helper in the serialization package gains a dependency on the Metadata API via the plain whole-module dotted import form: outside all requires subjects, zero-expectation probe of subject over-reach and import-form registration

from tamr_client._types.dataset import Dataset


def dataset_restore_target(dataset: Dataset) -> str:

    return f"restore{dataset.url.path}"

cases.grading_note: Zero violations expected: per ADR-0009 the helper's input type comes from the _types package, and a submodule import (from tamr_client._types.dataset import Dataset) is a dependency on the parent package tamr_client._types. The system fired nothing, and the case shows object-side ancestor matching WORKS: the module tamr_client._types.restore has no direct package-level _types import — both its HEAD import ('from tamr_client._types.url import URL') and the appended runtime import register submodule-form targets (tamr_client._types.url.URL, tamr_client._types.dataset.Dataset) — so the requires tamr_client.* -> tamr_client._types is satisfied only through the object-side ancestor tolerance in the engine (a reachable target matching object + '.' prefix counts as reachable). If that tolerance were dropped to exact object matching, the helper would flip to a fire and this case would catch it. Contrast with tamr-typechecking-import: there the guarded from-import names the package itself (tamr_client._types) and guard-agnostic extraction satisfies module scope; here the runtime import names a SUBMODULE and ancestor tolerance is what satisfies. Scope caveat, recorded for honesty: appending a helper into a _types module is outside ADR-0009's letter — no gold constraint encodes 'functions must not live in _types' — so zero expectations is the correct answer for the constraint set, and any future constraint in that direction would need re-curation of this case.

cases.description: New openid helper decodes ID-token payloads by hand, deliberately avoiding the oic library

diff.append:
import base64
import json


def parse_id_token(id_token):
    """Hand-rolled JWT payload decoding without the oic library (new code)."""
    payload_part = id_token.split(".")[1]
    padded = payload_part + "=" * (-len(payload_part) % 4)
    return json.loads(base64.b64decode(padded))

cases.grading_note: Zero violations expected under the module-scope reading of ADR-0009 (tuf-repository-helper precedent): openlobby/core/openid.py imports oic at module level, so openlobby.core.openid owns the required dependency and the requires is satisfied for every scope via enclosing-module seeding (#115). parse_id_token deliberately hand-rolls JWT decoding with base64/json and never touches oic, so the case discriminates a per-function-usage reading: a future scope change to per-function dependency usage would flip this case to a fire, and any ADR-0009 firing today would mean the #115 seeding regressed and counts as an over-trigger FP. The ADR-0002 elasticsearch and ADR-0012 django.db firings on parse_id_token are the recorded over-broad-subject FP classes (openid auth code is neither search code nor data access).

The system fired nothing, and the case is the import-form probe: 'from graphene import relay' does NOT register a dependency on graphene.relay in the initial parse_repo build (the from-import falls back to the module 'graphene' when the dotted target is unknown), but in this eval's augment path the import IS normalized — augment pass 2 re-walks the diff file against existing FQNs that include EXTERNAL nodes, and the graphene.relay external node exists (seeded by paginator.py's 'from graphene.relay import PageInfo' fallback edge), so openlobby.core.api.types gains IMPORTS graphene.relay and the function's enclosing-module seed satisfies ADR-0007's requires (#115). The case discriminates the augment-path behavior: if a future change made the augment path resolve from-imports only against repo-internal FQNs, or dropped the external-node fallback edges, requires graphene.relay would fire here as a false positive and the case would flip. cases.description: New middleware helper reads users through the Django ORM via the imported model: the sanctioned data access, without importing django.db
cases.grading_note: Zero violations expected: get_author_usernames accesses data exactly the way ADR-0012 mandates (PostgreSQL through the Django ORM: User.objects.filter on the module-imported model), and the ORM is the django.db access path, so a direct 'from django.db import ...' is not required for compliance. The system fired three requires violations at openlobby.core.middleware.get_author_usernames, all false positives, each documenting a distinct gap. (1) ADR-0012 requires django.db — the ORM-resolution FP and the reason this case exists: chained-call root resolution (#116) resolves User.objects to the internal class openlobby.core.models.User, whose only outward edge INHERITS the external django AbstractUser dead-end, so sanctioned ORM usage never registers a django.db dependency (same limitation class as the ADR-0012 firing documented in openlobby-search-orm-bypass). An ORM-resolution fix (mapping <Model>.objects usage to django.db) would collapse this FP and score the case clean. (2) ADR-0010 requires django — the recorded over-broad openlobby.* subject FP: middleware.py legitimately never imports django (it receives request objects and delegates to get_response). (3) ADR-0002 requires elasticsearch — the recorded over-broad openlobby.core.* subject FP: authentication middleware is not search code. Supersession holds: ADR-0006 requires flask stays quiet (superseded by ADR-0010, and middleware.py has no flask import).
